paragraphs.text: Separate read-only chat thread in the DeepSeek Harness right sidebar
# dsh-side-chat
English | Русский | 中文

A chat tab in the DeepSeek Harness right sidebar:
a **separate conversation** that sits next to your

working session, can read and search,
and **cannot change anything**.

Think of it as the AI chat you keep open in a browser tab — except it lives inside DSH,
already know
s which project you are in, and never touches your files.
## Why it exists

A DSH session *is* a chat, so why another one? Because the working session is a poor place
to ask "h

elp me think". Its transcript fills with tool calls, its context is spent on the
task, and every que
stion costs a turn in the middle of the work.
This plugin gives you a second thread that:

- runs its own session, so the two conversations never contaminate each other;
- inherits the workin

g directory, so it can actually look at the project you are in;
- is restricted to reading, so "just
check this file" never becomes "oops, edited it".
## Features

| **Separate thread** | Its own agent session, persisted across reloads and restarts |
| **Right-pan

el tab** | Opens next to your session, not instead of it |
| **Read-only** | `read`, `glob`, `grep`,

`read_image`, `web_search`, `web_fetch` — no write, no edit, no shell |
| **Streaming** | Answers a

ppear token by token, with a Stop button |
| **Reasoning level** | `off / low / high / max`, chosen

in Settings, applied per thread |
| **Voice input** | Records the microphone, transcribes through th

e host speech provider |
| **Images** | Attach screenshots; they are sent as prompt content parts |
| **Clean transcript** | Shows what was said, not the agent's internal monologue |
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x** with the Web UI (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`).
- A configured model prov

ider (any provider the host can route; the plugin uses your default).
- For voice: any speech provid

er registered in the host. Tested with a local
GigaAM provider; if no provider is
configured, the di
splay simply reports that nothing is available.
## Install

Then, from a DSH session, install the directory as a bundle (the tool performs package
installation
and bundle selection itself):

From the CLI the equivalent is:

One bundle installs **two** rows: the plugin and the agent preset it runs on (see
Why a preset ships
with it). There is no second step.
Then:

1. restart DSH, or toggle the plugin off and on in **Settings → Plugins**;
2. refresh the page (`F5`
) — the client half is a browser module.
To remove everything:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Use

**Open the panel** with the speech-bubble button in the conversation header, on the right
next to th
e session utilities. The tab also appears in the right sidebar's tab guide.
Inside the panel:

- **Type and press Enter.** Shift+Enter adds a line.
- **🎤 / mic** — record, press again to stop. Th

e transcript is appended to the draft,
so you can fix a word before sending.
- **Picture** — attach

images (several at once).
- **+** in the panel header — start a fresh thread. The old one keeps its
## Settings
**Settings → Plugins → Side chat** (and the plugin's own card in the plugins list).
### Reasoning level

How much the model thinks before answering: `Off`, `Low`, `High`, `Max`. The list comes
from the mod
el catalog, so it follows whichever model you run.

Default is `Off`: for a chat, reasoning tokens are the main cost and the main latency.
Switch to `Lo
w` or `High` if planning starts to feel shallow.

A note on the implementation: DSH's `selectModel` installs the choice on the session **and**
saves i

t as the deployment default in the background. The plugin restores the previous
default immediately

after, so your coding sessions keep their own level. The plugin reads
the value back from `GET /x-si

de-chat/models.json` — if `default.reasoningEffort` ever
changes, that restore step failed.
### Hide the Claude Migration button

Optional and **off by default**. `dsh-claude-move` injects a floating launcher as raw DOM,
not throu

gh a slot, so there is no registration to remove. The toggle adds one CSS rule
that hides it; the pl

ugin itself and its tools keep working. The preference lives in this
browser's `localStorage`.
## How it works
### Threads

The panel asks the **host** for a thread (`POST /x-side-chat/thread`). The host creates the
session

itself, which means it knows the id before the panel does and can apply the tool
mask in the same br

f, which means it knows the id before the panel does and can apply the tool
mask in the same breath.

The thread id is kept in the browser (`localStorage: dsh.side-chat.thread.v2`) and mirrored
in `$DSH

_HOME/side-chat/threads.json`. The registry exists so the mask can be re-applied on
`agent/created`
— a thread resumed after a restart is narrowed before its first turn.
### Why a preset ships with it

Agent presets decide what reaches the model. Created on a coding preset, the thread would
inherit th

e workspace `AGENTS.md`, the project rules and the entire skill catalog: it would
answer with report
s, task lists and tool talk, and cost several times more per turn.

The bundled `sidechat` preset mounts a persona, reading tools, web access and compaction —
and **not
** `agent-instructions`, `tool-skill` or any MCP server.
## Limitations

- A thread is a real DSH session: it appears in no workspace, but it does exist on disk and
is never

garbage-collected. Delete `$DSH_HOME/sessions/<id>` (or use your usual
quarantine) to drop one.
- T

he persona text is Russian. Edit the preset in `cordis.patch.yml` if you want another
language; the

UI itself follows the DSH locale.
- Tool steps are not shown as rows — a chat shows what was said, n

ot what ran.
- The runtime-context block (`Current working directory…`) is still sent to the model b

y a
host plugin; it is filtered out of the transcript but still costs tokens.
- Voice needs micropho
ne permission, and the first press may wait for the model to load.
